title: 110 recognised member releases in 58 functions stay refused by rule 5k's last-use premises (bodies that clear members without releasing the base, releases in loops, copies of the base)
why: Card W45-CALLEE-SUMMARY-CASCADE admits `B->F` at a Released { nullable } position only under the lexical premises P1-P4 of gateway constraint 5k (the base is a formal never copied; one release of the place and before it only null tests; no loop around it and no goto; the base released afterwards on every path), after its integration review measured that the unrestricted rule certified a double release Safe. Measured against the W44 call-argument census sink at base b160d765 (docs/reports/w45-callee-summary-cascade/census/residual-releases.json, scripts/residual_releases.py): of 137 statements in reported rows that the lexical gate refused and whose actual is a recognised pointer read at a Released position, 27 are admitted and 110, in 58 functions, stay refused (free 51, rd_free 32, mk_mem_free 14, flb_free 8, cfl_sds_destroy 2, rd_kafkap_str_destroy 2, the non-null ctr_destroy 1). The largest are rd_kafka_group_list_destroy (11, a loop over an array of members), mk_config_free_all (10) and flb_input_chunk_map (8). Clear-style bodies (rd_kafka_metadata_partition_clear, rd_kafka_snappy_free_env) release members without releasing the base, and no summary mode can state what they release. Discharge condition: either a place-level released fact keyed by base identity and member, sound under the fixed point and under aliasing, or a summary form stating the members a body releases through a formal with a caller-side record of it, each with Lean parity and a measured arbiter.

title: 254 member actuals at a Released position are refused by the typed recogniser before rule 5k is consulted (typedef record pointers, typedef pointer members, unread declarations)
why: Card W45-CALLEE-SUMMARY-CASCADE's census of the W44 call-argument sink at base b160d765 (docs/reports/w45-callee-summary-cascade/census/release-positions.json) counts 490 distinct refused actuals at Released positions: 138 recognised pointer reads, and 352 the recogniser refuses: untyped-base 112 (a base declared through a typedef of a record pointer, e.g. `rd_kafka_Node_t *node` in rd_kafka_Node_destroy), unreadable 75 (the function's declarations were not all read), untyped-member 67 (a member declared through a typedef of a pointer, e.g. `cfl_sds_t buf` in ctr_id_destroy and destroy_label), chain 89 (W45-MEMBER-RELEASE-CHAINS), cast 6, other 2, scalar 1. These hold the next destructor bodies of the cascade. Discharge condition: the typed declaration reader resolves typedef names of record pointers and pointer members (TypedAccessModel / FunctionTypes, shared by every typed route, so re-measured across all of them), with Lean parity for any changed premise and a measured arbiter; every newly recognised release still passes rule 5k's premises.

title: 89 member-chain actuals (`a->b->c`) at a Released position keep the refusal
why: Card W45-CALLEE-SUMMARY-CASCADE's rule 1 admits only the exact `B->F` shape of a formal `B`; 89 distinct refused actuals at Released positions are chains (census/release-positions.json). A chain release needs the last-use premises of gateway constraint 5k for the intermediate place as well as for the released one. Discharge condition: admit a chain actual at a nullable release with every link's W44-INDIRECT-CHAIN-ACCESS obligation and 5k's premises stated for the chain place, with Lean parity and a measured arbiter.

title: 411 Unknown functions remain blocked only by uncontracted calls; the cascade census ranks what would unblock them
why: Card W45-CALLEE-SUMMARY-CASCADE built the call graph of uncontracted-call leaves on Unknown functions (census/cascade-base.json.gz, cascade-after.json.gz; scripts/cascade.py). After the card: 4,509 Unknown functions, 2,613 with 9,194 uncontracted-call leaves, 411 blocked by nothing else, 299 by exactly one callee. Single-callee leverage is small (at most 12 functions, LZ4_decompress_generic); a cross-unit route over existing Safe home bodies would unblock 2 (not built); removing the indirect-access family from callee bodies would unblock 200 (186 before the card), the return-expression family 37, branch conditions 11. Of the 412 roots at base, 253 need a callee with no same-unit body. Discharge condition: none by one route; each card that models a callee-body family re-runs scripts/cascade.py and reports the move of this figure.
